cemc-gauss8-2007-03.title: Read each day
cemc-gauss8-2007-03.body:
From the graph (high, low, difference): Monday 20°, 10°, 10°; Tuesday 20°, 15°, 5°; Wednesday 25°, 25°, 0°; Thursday 30°, 10°, 20°; Friday 25°, 20°, 5°.

The greatest difference is on Thursday.

**Answer: (D) Thursday**

cemc-gauss8-2007-04.title: Favourable over total
cemc-gauss8-2007-04.body:
There are 6 equally likely faces and 2 of them (5 and 6) are favourable: $\frac{2}{6} = \frac{1}{3}$.

**Answer: (C) $\frac{1}{3}$**

cemc-gauss8-2007-05.title: Cube root
cemc-gauss8-2007-05.body:
The volume of a cube with edge $x$ is $x^3$. So $x^3 = 8$, and since $2 \times 2 \times 2 = 8$, $x = 2$.

**Answer: (A) 2**

cemc-gauss8-2007-06.title: Unit rate
cemc-gauss8-2007-06.body:
The rate is $18 \div 3 = 6$ cents per minute, so 10 minutes cost 60 cents $= \$0.60$.

**Answer: (B) \$0.60**

cemc-gauss8-2007-06.title: Scale up
cemc-gauss8-2007-06.body:
9 minutes is 3 times as long, costing $3 \times 18 = 54$ cents; one more minute (6 cents) makes 60 cents.

**Answer: (B) \$0.60**

cemc-gauss8-2007-10.title: Order the digits
cemc-gauss8-2007-10.body:
Largest: digits in decreasing order, 951. Smallest: increasing order, 159. Difference: $951 - 159 = 792$.

**Answer: (C) 792**

cemc-gauss8-2007-12.title: Isosceles triangles
cemc-gauss8-2007-12.body:
$\triangle ADC$ is isosceles ($AD = DC$), so $\angle DAC = \angle DCA = 40^\circ$ and $\angle ADC = 100^\circ$. Then $\angle ADB = 180^\circ - 100^\circ = 80^\circ$. $\triangle ADB$ is isosceles ($AD = DB$), so $\angle BAD = \frac{1}{2}(180^\circ - 80^\circ) = 50^\circ$.

$\angle BAC = 50^\circ + 40^\circ = 90^\circ$.

**Answer: (D) $90^\circ$**

cemc-gauss8-2007-12.title: Angle sum shortcut
cemc-gauss8-2007-12.body:
Let $\angle BAD = \angle ABD = a$ and $\angle DAC = \angle DCA = b$ (two isosceles triangles). The angles of $\triangle ABC$ are $a$, $b$ and $a + b$, so $2(a + b) = 180^\circ$ and $\angle BAC = a + b = 90^\circ$.

**Answer: (D) $90^\circ$**

cemc-gauss8-2007-13.title: Multiplication principle
cemc-gauss8-2007-13.body:
Each art choice can go with each sports choice and each music choice: $2 \times 3 \times 4 = 24$.

**Answer: (B) 24**

cemc-gauss8-2007-14.title: Compare decimals
cemc-gauss8-2007-14.body:
$\frac{17}{100} = 0.17$. The choices are $0.25$, $0.2$, $0.1\overline{6}$, $0.142\ldots$, $0.125$. The closest is $\frac{1}{6} \approx 0.167$.

**Answer: (C) $\frac{1}{6}$**

cemc-gauss8-2007-15.title: All remainders appear
cemc-gauss8-2007-15.body:
Among any four consecutive integers, exactly one leaves each of the remainders 0, 1, 2, 3 when divided by 4. So the sum is $0 + 1 + 2 + 3 = 6$.

**Answer: (A) 6**

cemc-gauss8-2007-15.title: Try an example
cemc-gauss8-2007-15.body:
With 5, 6, 7, 8 the remainders are 1, 2, 3, 0, which add to 6.

**Answer: (A) 6**

cemc-gauss8-2007-16.title: Use the formulas
cemc-gauss8-2007-16.body:
With radius $r$: area $\pi r^2$, circumference $2\pi r$. With radius $3r$: area $\pi (3r)^2 = 9\pi r^2$ (9 times) and circumference $2\pi(3r) = 3 \times 2\pi r$ (3 times).

**Answer: (A)**

cemc-gauss8-2007-17.title: Set up an equation
cemc-gauss8-2007-17.body:
Work in thousands. If the winner got $x$, the others got $x - 22$, $x - 30$, $x - 73$. Then $4x - 125 = 5219$, so $4x = 5344$ and $x = 1336$. The winner got 1 336 000 votes.

**Answer: (D) 1 336 000**

cemc-gauss8-2007-17.title: Add back the gaps
cemc-gauss8-2007-17.body:
If everyone had as many votes as the winner, the total would be $5219 + 22 + 30 + 73 = 5344$ thousand. Divide by 4: 1336 thousand.

**Answer: (D) 1 336 000**

cemc-gauss8-2007-19.title: Big over small
cemc-gauss8-2007-19.body:
All four numbers are positive and $w < x < y < z$. A fraction is largest when its numerator is largest and its denominator is smallest, so $\frac{z}{w}$ is the largest.

**Answer: (E) $\frac{z}{w}$**

cemc-gauss8-2007-20.title: Total distance over total time
cemc-gauss8-2007-20.body:
Going: $240 \div 120 = 2$ h. Returning: $240 \div 80 = 3$ h. Total: 480 km in 5 h, so $480 \div 5 = 96$ km/h.

**Answer: (B) 96**

cemc-gauss8-2007-20.title: Average hour by hour
cemc-gauss8-2007-20.body:
Her speeds in the 5 hours were 120, 120, 80, 80, 80, which average to $480 \div 5 = 96$ km/h. (Not 100, because she spent more time at the slower speed.)

**Answer: (B) 96**

cemc-gauss8-2007-21.title: Area of the overlap
cemc-gauss8-2007-21.body:
The area of $WXYZ$ is $10 \times 6 = 60$, so the shaded area is 30. The shaded region is a rectangle with width $DC = 6$ and height $PD$, so $6 \times PD = 30$ and $PD = 5$. Then $AP = 6 - 5 = 1$.

**Answer: (A) 1**

cemc-gauss8-2007-22.title: Main sector plus a small one
cemc-gauss8-2007-22.body:
With the leash fully out, Chuck can sweep $270^\circ$ around the corner (the shed blocks the other $90^\circ$): area $\frac{3}{4} \times \pi \times 3^2 = \frac{27}{4}\pi$.

Along the 3 m side the leash just reaches the far corner, so nothing more there. Along the 2 m side, 1 m of leash is left at the far corner, so Chuck can swing around it in a $90^\circ$ sector of radius 1: $\frac{1}{4}\pi$.

Total: $\frac{27}{4}\pi + \frac{1}{4}\pi = 7\pi$ m².

**Answer: (A) $7\pi$ m²**

cemc-gauss8-2007-23.title: Count the \$5 bills
cemc-gauss8-2007-23.body:
The amount in \$5 bills must be odd (since $207 -$ an even amount is odd), so it ends in 5: 5, 15, 25, …, 205. Each leaves an even remainder that \$2 coins can fill. Dropping the final 5 from each leaves 0, 1, 2, …, 20, so there are 21 such amounts.

**Answer: (E) 21**

cemc-gauss8-2007-23.title: Trade bills for coins
cemc-gauss8-2007-23.body:
Start with 1 coin and 41 bills. Trading two \$5 bills for five \$2 coins keeps the total. The number of bills can be 41, 39, 37, …, 1 — all the odd numbers from 1 to 41, which is 21 ways.

**Answer: (E) 21**

cemc-gauss8-2007-24.title: Step along each side
cemc-gauss8-2007-24.body:
From $(2,1)$ to $(12,21)$: 10 right, 20 up, so 2 up per 1 right — a lattice point at every $x$ from 2 to 12: 11 points.

From $(2,1)$ to $(17,6)$: 15 right, 5 up, so 3 right per 1 up: 6 points.

From $(12,21)$ to $(17,6)$: 5 right, 15 down: 6 points.

The 3 vertices were each counted twice: $11 + 6 + 6 - 3 = 20$.

**Answer: (C) 20**

cemc-gauss8-2007-24.title: Use the gcd
cemc-gauss8-2007-24.body:
A segment with horizontal change $a$ and vertical change $b$ contains $\gcd(a,b)$ lattice steps. The sides give $\gcd(10,20) = 10$, $\gcd(15,5) = 5$, $\gcd(5,15) = 5$. Going around the perimeter, the number of lattice points equals the number of steps: $10 + 5 + 5 = 20$.

**Answer: (C) 20**

cemc-gauss8-2007-25.title: Big triangle minus small triangle
cemc-gauss8-2007-25.body:
Area $DRQC$ = area $\triangle PDC$ − area $\triangle PRQ$.

The first fold puts $C$ onto $AD$, so $PC = DC = 5$ and $\triangle PDC$ is a right isosceles triangle: area $\frac{1}{2} \times 5 \times 5 = 12.5$, and $\angle DPC = 45^\circ$.

Similarly $BQ = AB = 5$ and $\angle AQB = 45^\circ$. On $BC = 8$: $BP = 8 - 5 = 3$ and $QC = 3$, so $PQ = 8 - 3 - 3 = 2$.

$\triangle PRQ$ has two $45^\circ$ angles, so it is a right isosceles triangle with hypotenuse 2. Four copies make a square of side 2, so its area is $\frac{4}{4} = 1$.

Area $DRQC = 12.5 - 1 = 11.5$ cm².

**Answer: (D) 11.5**
